title: Optimization for Machine Learning (lecture notes)
byline: Bernd Gärtner (ETH) and Martin Jaggi (EPFL) · CS-439, Spring 2023
note: Course notes; PDF page = printed page + 1. Exercises at the end of each chapter are not broken down. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A proof-oriented course on the first-order and second-order methods behind machine-learning training. After a self-contained chapter on convex sets and functions, each chapter takes one algorithm and proves how many steps it needs under which assumptions: gradient descent for Lipschitz, smooth and strongly convex objectives (with Nesterov acceleration), projected and proximal variants for constraints and nonsmooth regularizers, subgradient and stochastic gradient descent, what can still be said for nonconvex functions, Newton and quasi-Newton (BFGS) methods, coordinate descent, and the projection-free Frank–Wolfe algorithm. The recurring pattern is a short “vanilla analysis” sharpened by each extra assumption into a better rate.
